socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced a new 2026 ARC-AGI-2 Kaggle high of 88.06% by Tufa Labs and said a $150,000 bonus would be split among teams scoring above 85%.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A public-board threshold announcement and major standings lead; the post does not establish a final private score.

socialPosts.author: masspeakss
socialPosts.summary: masspeaks reacted in Japanese to Tufa Labs exceeding 85% on ARC-AGI-2, calling the result impressive. The public board independently shows Tufa Labs at 88.06% in the afternoon snapshot.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Respectful reaction from a current ARC-AGI-2 mover to the leader.

socialPosts.author: masspeakss
socialPosts.summary: In a Japanese post, masspeaks said careful preparation had paid off and expected a high gold-band cutoff. This is the contestant’s reaction; the post alone does not establish the exact score or method.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Context from the ARC-AGI-2 public-board mover; compare any score or rank with the board brief.

socialPosts.author: tufalabs
socialPosts.summary: In a reply to Mike Knoop’s ARC-AGI-2 bonus-threshold post, Tufa Labs said it had not set out to solve ARC-AGI-2, started by accident, and plans to share more after the deadline. This is the team’s account, not an independently established history.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: First-person context from the ARC-AGI-2 public-board leader; no method or final result is disclosed.

socialPosts.author: JFPuget
socialPosts.summary: Puget asked ARC Prize whether the 85% bonus threshold refers to the public or private leaderboard; no organizer answer was visible in the checked thread.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Flags a reporting question; avoid presenting the public score as the final prize result.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop said ARC-AGI-2 remains much harder than ARC-AGI-1 and that eventual open solutions will be useful to study, while quoting his earlier reaction to Tufa Labs crossing the public Kaggle bonus threshold.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Organizer context about the contest; his forward-looking statement is not a released solution or final award.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop said the 85% Grand Prize bonus threshold had been reached on Kaggle and called 2026 the final ARC-AGI-2 Kaggle year.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Provides organizer context for the Tufa Labs result; his expectation about future open artifacts is not yet a release.

socialPosts.author: fchollet
socialPosts.summary: Chollet reacted to ARC Prize’s Tufa Labs ARC-2 announcement by saying Kaggle scores are getting very good.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A founder reaction adds a measured voice to the organizer’s score announcement.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced Stephen Wolfram as a keynote speaker for its 2026 Research Summit.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A current event-program lead for the meeting digest.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize published verified Grok 4.7 scores: 1.8% on ARC-AGI-3 with its standard harness, 10.0% with a provider adapter, and 61.4% on ARC-AGI-2.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: The harness distinction matters when comparing model scores; the post reports organizer verification.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize published verified DeepSeek V4.1 Flash scores of 72.9% on ARC-AGI-2 and 94.5% on ARC-AGI-1, with stated per-task costs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A dated organizer model verification relevant to ARC-2 comparisons.

wireStories.headline: MINAGI leaps from 862nd to 19th on ARC-2

sections.text: MINAGI added 10.00 points to reach 40.14, jumping from 862nd to 19th in the past day. The current gold cutoff is 41.81, with 15 teams in the gold places.
The standings now place MINAGI near the medal positions after starting well outside the top 100. The public board is provisional, with medals decided on the private board.
